sn15.20:2.3: For Vepulla, see [sn15.10:2.2](). | A _pācīnavaṁsa_ was a hall or shed built for the ritual, with bamboo (_vaṁsa_) beams running easterly (_pācīna_; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 3.1.1.6 and Eggeling’s note). Perhaps the mountain was noted as the site for the introduction of this ritual institution. In the Buddha’s day, there was a “Park of the East-Raftered Hall” in Cetī ([mn128:8.1](), [an8.30:1.2]()).
sn15.20:2.4: _Tivara_ may be connected to Vedic _trivarūtha_, the “triple defence”. This may be connected with the fortifications for which Rājagaha is famous. But by Vedic times it acquired a religious sense, here suggesting the people who have the protection of the gods due to their correct performance of the ritual in their hall. The “triple defence” can be seen as a precursor of the Buddhist triple refuge.
sn15.20:2.8: The pairs of disciples are listed at [dn14:1.9.1](). A story of Sañjīva is given at [mn50:9.2]().
sn15.20:3.2: These two terms are found in Rig Veda 4.6.9, “red horses going straight, going well” (_rohitāsa ṛjvañcaḥ svañcaḥ_), where _rohitassa_ is the “red horse” of the sunbeams ([sn2.26]()), and Sanskrit _vañca_ is evidently found in Pali _vaṅka_ in the sense “going” (unless it is from _vañcati_, “fire”). Perhaps the mountain, which lies to the east of the city, was named for the flashing beams of sunlight at dawn.
sn15.20:4.1: _Supassa_ is “Fairslope”, a name used for several mountains, including one on the eastern side of mount Meru.
sn15.20:5.5: Kauṭilya says there are fifteen _muhuttas_ (Sanskrit _muhūrta_) per day, and fifteen per night, making 48 minutes (Arthaśāstra 2.20.37).
